name: John Joseph Quinn
notable_stories: A communication specialist in WWI who rolled out wires between battlefields; he suffered from shell shock and PTSD, having been kicked by his assistant mule during action
Returned from WWI unable to work due to the noise at the Continental Can Factory
Opened his home to orphans Barbara Adams and Chuck McKeldin
WWI veteran: shell-shocked, mustard-gassed once (survived via fast gas-mask response), worked as communication/wireline expert using a mule to route wires to combat-zone headquarters
Per Barbara p. 58: never worked a day in his life after WWI (likely meaning no fixed paid employment post-war)
Barbara's great-uncle (Ethel's youngest brother) and functional step-grandfather after Buckey married Peggy

Ethel's sister Margaret (b. 1905) was younger than him, so he was the youngest brother rather than the youngest sibling.

Married Marie Ellinghaus on 25 May 1925 at St Ann's Church, Baltimore (Quinn Family Tree on Ancestry). Children: Margaret Frances "Peggy" (1927), Catherine Joan (1930), John Joseph Jr. (1934) and Patricia Marie "Pat" (1940).
